translation.en: For Jātavedas (Agni) [the lord of the beings] we shall extract soma to burn down the wealth of the enemy. He is passing our society over impediments. As with a boat Agni always passes the sea of danger.

entries.meaning: Jātavedas — Agni, the knower of all created beings

entries.note: 1st pl. subjunctive of √su 'to extract/press'

entries.meaning: of the hostile / envious one (the enemy)
entries.note: gen. sg. of the denominative participle arātīyát- 'behaving as an enemy'; the word runs over the line-break — its final syllables (-yataḥ) fall on the next word
final syllables -yataḥ of arātīyataḥ, carried over from the previous line
preverb of dahāti ('burns down')
ni-dahāti: '(Agni) burns down (the foe's wealth)'
logical object of dahāti — '(he) burns the wealth (of the enemy)'
enclitic accusative naḥ
s-aorist subjunctive of √pṛ 'to take across, rescue'
agrees with durgāṇi

translation.en: Her fire complexion is hot as solar blaze. She is honoured by the fruits of action. Goddess Durgā, I surrender to your refuge, you sail kindly. Obeisance to the skipper.

entries.note: bahuvrīhi 'having the hue of fire'; the compound spans the line-break, its ending -varṇāṁ falls on the next word
second member -varṇāṁ of agni-varṇāṁ, carried over from the previous line
pres. act. participle of √jval 'to blaze', acc. sg. f.
uninflected prior member of the compound karma-phala 'fruit of action'
loc. pl.; second member of karma-phaleṣu 'in the fruits of action'
ppp of √juṣ, acc. sg. f.
pra + √pad 'to resort to'; ātmanepada pra-padye
su- 'well' + tarasi (2nd sg. of √tṝ 'to cross over')
dat. sg. of taras 'energy, crossing'; 'tarase namaḥ' = homage for safe passage. (Some read tarase as a 2nd-person verb of √tṝ.)

translation.en: O Agni, you are fit to be praised. All of us with our fortunes always pass over impediments. Purify the earth, may our fields be abundant, and our children and grandchildren happy.

entries.note: imperative 2nd sg. of the causative pāráyati of √pṛ 'to take across' (Vedic lengthened pārayā)
here adverbially 'anew'; some derive it as a gerundive of √nu 'to praise'
acc. pl. asmān (euphonic -th before sv-)
agrees with durgāṇi
pūḥ (nom. sg.) → pūś before ca-: 'be thou a fortress for us'

entries.meaning: broad, wide, ample (also: the wide Earth)

entries.note: naḥ (encl. dat./gen. pl.), shortened to na before u-
imperative 2nd sg. (Vedic lengthened bhavā)
paired with toka: 'children and grandchildren'
indeclinable, paired with yoḥ
archaic (from noun yu); śaṁ-yoḥ = 'weal and welfare'

translation.en: May Jātavedas carry us across all these dangers, as if crossing a sea of difficulties with a boat. Praising you a Agni with an elevated mind, like Atri, that invocation will protect our bodies.

entries.note: viśvāni (durgāṇi) 'all the perils'
enclitic naḥ (object of parṣi)
voc. sg.; 'thou who slayest the perils'

entries.meaning: O Jātavedas (Agni, knower of all beings)

entries.note: sindhum
Vedic comparative particle na (= iva)
2nd sg. s-aorist subjunctive of √pṛ 'to take (us) across'

entries.meaning: like Atri (as for the sage Atri)
entries.note: taddhita -vat 'like'; 'as thou didst for Atri'
pres. mid. part. of √gṝ 'to invoke, praise'
Vedic imperative bodhi 'be!'; some derive it from √budh 'be attentive'

translation.en: Men in battle invoke proud victory of fierce Agni from the highest regions. He is a patient god passing our society over impediments. Agni always carries over grim dangers.

entries.note: uninflected prior member of pṛtanā-jit 'conquering in battles'
pṛtanā-jítam, acc. sg. — epithet of Agni
pres. mid. part. of √sah 'to prevail'
1st pl. optative of √hū/hve 'to call, invoke' (huvema)
abl. sg., agrees with sadhasthāt
abl. sg. — 'from the highest abode'
enclitic accusative naḥ
s-aorist subjunctive of √pṛ 'to take across, rescue'
obscure in this context; taken as abl. of kṣām 'earth'. Some reciters/editions read it together with devaḥ as an epithet of the resplendent Agni. Meaning uncertain.
the recitation sets 'ati' off with a pause before 'duritā … agniḥ'
the linking -ty- is the tail of the preceding 'ati' (ati + agniḥ → aty agniḥ)

accented: sa̱nāc ca̱ hotā̱ navyaś̍ ca̱ sathsi̍ |
lines: sanāc ca hotā navyaś ca sathsi |

translation.en: You are ancient indeed, well invoked in sacrifices. You sit and the priest always praises you. Agni and Herself should have been delighted. Now sacrifice and grant prosperity to all of us!

entries.note: recited pratnoṣi = pratnaḥ hi (RV 8.11.10); some read pratno 'si 'thou art ancient'
Vedic enclitic particle, often after hi

entries.meaning: from of old, from ancient times, ever

entries.note: 'sanāt … navyaḥ' = both of old and anew
satsi, 2nd sg. of √sad 'to sit, take one's seat'
svāṁ (agrees with tanuvam)
'thine own body'
piprayasva, reduplicated imperative mid. 2nd sg. of √prī 'to please'
asmabhyam, dat. pl.
preverb of ā-yajasva 'procure by worship'
ā + √yaj; ā-yajasva 'obtain for us by thy sacrifice'

translation.en: O Indra, adorned with the matchless sprinkled flocks of stars from Viṣṇu, we may roam together with you, over the top of the sky. May She be glad living together with us here in the heaven of Lord Viṣṇu.

entries.note: ppp of √juṣ; juṣṭam
'having no equal' — epithet of Indra/Viṣṇu; case ambiguous (taken as gen.)
ni-sikta, acc. sg.; niṣiktam
tava, gen. sg.
